title: Neural-network-ranked survey found candidate lenses and spectroscopically followed seven
summary: Two residual neural networks ranked multiband UNIONS galaxy images for strong-lens candidates; researchers visually graded the candidates. The paper lists 1,346 candidates and reports independent Keck/Gemini spectroscopy for seven selected high-quality systems, with background-source redshifts above 2.1. The authors report overlaps with other lens surveys. This entry represents one AI-assisted survey and its selected spectroscopic follow-up, not 1,346 confirmed lenses or seven uniquely first-discovered objects; object-level priority and complete cross-survey overlap remain unresolved.
ai_technology: Two residual neural networks trained on real lens images and applied to multiband UNIONS imaging
organization: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa; Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory; University of San Francisco; University of California, Berkeley; Université Paris-Saclay; Laboratoire d’Astrophysique de Marseille; National Research Council Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics; University of Waterloo; Perimeter Institute; University of British Columbia

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 full paper and history; authors’ primary candidate-catalog deposit and later dataset record for coordinates, overlaps and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The paper reports 1,346 human-reviewed lens candidates and spectroscopy of seven selected high-quality systems with background-source redshifts above 2.1.
evidence.unknown: Candidates overlap other surveys; not every candidate is spectroscopically confirmed, and full object-level priority/cross-survey matching is not claimed.
evidence.ai_role: Residual neural networks ranked imaging candidates for human inspection and selection for spectroscopic follow-up.
